why: B (Corollary 6.7 for a closed slice M ⊆ ℝ^{K+1}, dim ≥ 1): some smooth f on M has no degenerate critical point and compact sublevel sets. A ⇒ B is A's exists_isMorseFunction_isCompact_sublevel. B ⇒ A is proved, but only partly from B: the existence clauses (Morse f with compact sublevels; with finitely many critical points per sublevel; finitely many critical points on compact M) follow from B (dim 0 / empty M by L_p) plus the project's IsMorseFunction.finite_inter_setOf_isCriticalPointM (critical points of a Morse function are isolated). A's other two clauses carry Milnor's proof, not his statement: compactness of sublevels of L_p on closed M (elementary, re-proved) and 'a.e. p gives a Morse L_p with compact sublevels', which B_to_A takes from the project's ae_isMorseFunction_normSq_sub (V4_12) without using B. As propositions they are equivalent given the project; in content A additionally contains the a.e.-p form of the construction (Theorem 6.6 for closed M) and finiteness of critical points per sublevel.
